thesis.reason: The trend indicators line up bullish. The 50-day EMA (about 79,889) sits above the 200-day EMA (about 75,380), which sits above the 200-day SMA (about 71,954), so shorter-term price momentum is stacked above longer-term averages. ADX at about 35 means the trend is strong, not just drifting. RSI(2) at about 42 means the market has pulled back a bit without becoming overbought, which can offer an entry closer to trend support than a chase after a spike. Volatility is low (ATR% rank 0.2), so the stop can sit tighter relative to the move. The headlines are mixed (a 'dip below $83,000' warning, an OpenAI-related selloff, a bullish TD Cowen forecast), so they don't clearly confirm or refute the trend. The indicator snapshot may not match the current price, so verify the live price against the EMA levels before relying on this.
invalidation: A daily close below the 200-day EMA (about 75,380) would mean the long-term trend has broken.
A daily close below the 50-day EMA (about 79,889) that isn't reclaimed within about 5 sessions would show the pullback is turning into a reversal.
The 50-day EMA crossing below the 200-day EMA (a 'death cross') would mean the moving-average structure has flipped bearish.
ADX falling below about 20 while price chops around the 50-day EMA would mean the trend has lost strength and the TREND signal is no longer valid.
